purpose: Defines what may execute as part of Biology. Gameplay and presentation behavior must be project-original; source mods are reference material only. Biology is vanilla-first: preserve CDPR identities/surfaces where useful and substitute project-original mechanics beneath them.

releaseExperience.note: Internal module gates may exist during development and acceptance, but a release build enables the complete accepted Biology experience as one product. The only in-game public preference is Biology's save-persistent E3-inspired first-person HUD/nameplate Boolean; it does not change simulation authority or whole-mod activation.

vanillaFirst.rule: Keep vanilla item/system names, identities, animations, screens/assets and interaction language where they can host the realism model. Replace mechanics underneath instead of importing source-mod renames or duplicating the vanilla surface.

runtimeOwnership.frameworkRule: A framework may expose APIs, script loading, data loading, UI primitives or input plumbing. It may not supply the body, combat, injury, armor, presentation or progression behavior that defines Biology.
runtimeOwnership.referenceRule: Third-party gameplay/presentation mods may be studied and retained as provenance/reference records, but their scripts, archives, tweak payloads and assets may not be required by or packaged into the standalone Biology runtime. The E3 visual target must therefore be recreated in Biology-owned code/assets rather than executed from the source mod.

genericInfrastructure.settingsBoundary: The remaining E3-inspired presentation Boolean is persisted by Biology's CRRealpassSettings ScriptableSystem and edited from Biology-owned body-shell Ink UI. REDlauncher/REDmod is the sole whole-mod activation boundary. No external settings provider or pause-menu provider registration is part of the production runtime.

developmentRules: Internal modules may be independently gated to isolate faults and calibrate systems.
Development gates are not player preferences and must not become a release configuration menu.
A development candidate advertised as owned-runtime must fail closed if Dark Future, Project E3, Mod Settings, ArchiveXL or RED4ext executing content is present in its production deployment manifest.
A development candidate advertised as owned-runtime must preserve vanilla item/system identity and reject inherited source-mod item renames.
The current owned candidate may stage only redscript as generic runtime infrastructure; adding another framework requires a concrete current consumer and synchronized contract change.
Reference recipes may remain in the repository for historical provenance but may not feed the standalone owned-runtime builder.
No source-mod save state may be required to initialize a clean Biology save/runtime.
releaseRules: The accepted body, injury, combat, armor, cyberware-physiology and presentation authorities ship together.
The release has one authored balance rather than exposing subsystem disable switches.
The sole in-game public preference may disable the Biology-owned E3-inspired HUD/nameplate visual skin only; it cannot change simulation or whole-mod activation.
REDlauncher/REDmod is the sole whole-mod public activation boundary.
Traditional actor health bars are intentionally not part of the final authored Biology presentation once replacement feedback is accepted.
External gameplay/presentation mods are optional user choices outside Biology and are not prerequisites, bundled payloads or hidden runtime hosts.
Generic framework dependencies may be bundled only when explicitly required as infrastructure and properly licensed/noticed; they never become gameplay/presentation policy owners.
Vanilla item/system identities are preserved unless a future explicit product goal authorizes a replacement identity.
Every runtime file in the Biology-owned payload must have explicit provenance.
